See also: sinagogă

Asturian

[edit]
Asturian Wikipedia has an article on:
sinagoga
Wikipedia ast

Etymology

[edit]

From Late Latin synagōga, from Ancient Greek συναγωγή (sunagōgḗ, “assembly”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /sinaˈɡoɡa/ [si.naˈɡo.ɡa]
  • Rhymes: -oɡa
  • Syllabification: si‧na‧go‧ga

Noun

[edit]

sinagoga f (plural sinagogues)

  1. synagogue (place)

Further reading

[edit]
  • “sinagoga”, in Diccionariu de la llingua asturiana [Dictionary of the Asturian Language] (in Asturian), 1st edition, Academy of the Asturian Language [Asturian: Academia de la Llingua Asturiana], 2000, →ISBN

Ladino

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Late Latin synagōga, from Ancient Greek συναγωγή (sunagōgḗ) "assembly, gathering", from συνάγω (sunágō) "I bring together". Doublet of esnoga.

Noun

[edit]

sinagoga f (plural sinagogas)

  1. (Judaism) synagogue

Synonyms

[edit]
  • esnoga (אסנוגה)

Etymology

[edit]
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *sem-der.?
Proto-Hellenic *ksún
Ancient Greek σῠ́ν (sŭ́n)
Ancient Greek συν- (sun-)
Proto-Indo-European *h₂eǵ-
Proto-Indo-European *h₂éǵeti
Proto-Hellenic *ágō
Ancient Greek ἄγω (ágō)
Ancient Greek συνάγω (sunágō)
Proto-Indo-European *-h₂
Proto-Indo-European *-éh₂
Ancient Greek -ᾱ (-ā)
Ancient Greek -ή (-ḗ)
Ancient Greek συναγωγή (sunagōgḗ)bor.
Latin synagōgalbor.
Old Galician-Portuguese sinagoga

    Learned borrowing from Latin synagōga, borrowed from Ancient Greek συναγωγή (sunagōgḗ), from συνάγω (sunágō) + -ή (-ḗ).

    Noun

    [edit]

    sinagoga f (plural sinagogas)

    1. synagogue
      • a. 1284, Alfonso X of Castile, Cantigas de Santa Maria, Códice rico, cantiga 27 (facsimile), page 41v:
        C.õ oſ aptos cprꝛon a ſinagoga dꝯ judeꝯ pera fazer eigreia d. ſ. m.
        [C[om]o os ap[os]t[olo]s c[om]pr[a]ron a sinagoga dos judeos pera fazer eigreja d[e] S[anta] M[aria].]
        How the Apostles bought the synagogue to make the Church of Saint Mary.

    Descendants

    [edit]
    • Fala: sinagoga
    • Galician: sinagoga
    • Portuguese: sinagoga

    Portuguese sinagoga

      Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese sinagoga, from Latin synagōga, from Ancient Greek συναγωγή (sunagōgḗ, “assembly, gathering”), from συνάγω (sunágō, “to bring together”).

      Pronunciation

      [edit]
       
      • (Brazil) IPA(key): /si.naˈɡɔ.ɡɐ/
      • (Brazil) IPA(key): /si.naˈɡɔ.ɡɐ/
        • (Southern Brazil) IPA(key): /si.naˈɡɔ.ɡa/
      • (Portugal) IPA(key): /si.nɐˈɡɔ.ɡɐ/ [si.nɐˈɣɔ.ɣɐ]

      • Audio (Brazil (Caipira)):(file)
      • Rhymes: -ɔɡɐ
      • Hyphenation: si‧na‧go‧ga

      Noun

      [edit]

      sinagoga f (plural sinagogas)

      1. synagogue
